body: Monday, March 03 2025 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2025-03-03 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: Growth data softened into the report date while markets priced a slower path rather than a recession. The January PCE index rose 2.5%, in line with expectations [1], and the Fed’s preferred core gauge hit 2.6% [2], so inflation is not what is breaking the tape. Activity is. The Atlanta Fed indicator put first-quarter growth on track to be negative [3], and its nowcast saw the economy shrinking after Friday’s data [4]. Households are pulling back: consumer confidence fell by the most since 2021 [5], spending posted its first drop in almost two years [6], and weekly jobless claims jumped to 242,000 [7]. Fourth-quarter GDP was still 2.3% annualized [8], so the slowdown is a late-winter story, not a finished one.

Rates & Curve: The 10-year Treasury closed February at 4.24% and the 2-year at 3.99%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 25 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28). Over 20 observations the 2-year fell 19 bps and the 10-year 28 bps, which leaves the spread 9 bps narrower. The curve is positively sloped and the move is a bull flattening, with the long end rallying more than the front. The five-observation move (2Y −20 bps, 10Y −18 bps; US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28) says the bid is recent and still running, and Bloomberg reported a Treasury rally that sent yields back below 4% as inflation cooled [9]. Equities did not follow the bonds. The S&P 500 closed at 5,954.50, down 1.9% over 20 sessions and 1.0% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The Nasdaq 100 is down 2.9% over 20 sessions, and the Russell 2000, at 2,163.07, is down 6.3%, the sharpest drawdown of the three. The VIX stands at 19.63, up 3.79 points over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and the dollar index at 107.61 is down 0.2% over 20 sessions but up 0.9% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).

New / Most Important: The tariff clock is the event to price. The administration has set March 4 for tariffs on Mexico and Canada, with the exact levels still to be set [10], and Trump has vowed an extra 10% on China over fentanyl in the same package [11]. Bessent says tariffs will not raise inflation [12], and that is the argument the bond market is buying: duties read as a growth tax rather than a price shock. Bessent has also promised an ‘affordability czar’ to deal with the cost effects [13]. For equities the threat already sits in the Russell 2000’s underperformance, which is where import-dependent and credit-sensitive companies trade.

Playbook ✓: Own duration into the jobs data and keep equity beta light. The bull flattening, with the 10-year down 28 bps over 20 sessions, says the bond market is pricing a softer labour market before the data confirm it. Reuters reports that investor angst about the economy will be tested by the next US jobs data [14], so the bid can extend if the print is weak. Add equity risk only when the Nasdaq 100 reclaims 21,508.12, its 20-session reference close, and the 10-year closes back above 4.52%, the level it held on January 30, which would be the sign the bond rally has run its course. Stay away from small caps until the tariff date has passed.

Macro Stance: Euro-area growth is slow but no longer choked by policy. ECB board member Schnabel said rates are no longer a material drag on growth [15], while Wunsch said the bank might have to lower its key rate to a level that stimulates the economy [16]. Germany is the weak link. The Bundesbank chief said the economy is five minutes to midnight after the central bank’s first loss in 45 years [17], and German business morale stagnated in February ahead of the election [18]. The euro is the transmission channel: EUR/USD closed at 1.0395, down 1.0% over five sessions and flat over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Reuters reported investors betting on the sharpest US–Europe inflation divergence since 2022 [19].

Credit & Inflation: S&P revised France’s outlook to negative [20], and Bloomberg framed it as a budget warning [21], which turns the sovereign spread into a periphery problem as well. Equities have looked through it for now. The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 5,463.54, up 3.3% over 20 sessions, and Germany’s DAX at 22,551.43 is up 3.8% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The STOXX 600 is up 3.3% over 20 sessions at 557.19 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The ECB’s patience has a reason: the euro-area and US inflation paths are diverging [19].

New / Most Important: The tariff is the event. Trump said 25% tariffs on the EU would be announced soon [22], and the Guardian warned the threat could trigger economic turmoil [23]. European shares already reacted, as Wall Street ended lower while tariff risk rattled them [24]. Europe is also trying to set its own terms on Ukraine. It agreed steps toward peace but needs US backing [25], and UK and European leaders are drafting a plan to take to Washington [26]. Germany’s politics complicate the defence side too, since East German voters complicate the Merz plan to boost Ukraine defence spending [27].

Playbook ✓: Own the defence bid as the hedge and treat a tariff announcement as the sell trigger for German cyclicals. Rheinmetall closed at EUR 1,006.50 after gaining 33.24% over 20 sessions and 12.56% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), so the trade is already crowded and the risk is a peace headline that removes the premium quickly. The DAX’s 3.8% gain over 20 sessions discounts a deal, which makes a 25% announcement the test [22]. Avoid French banks and autos until the S&P outlook cut is absorbed, and treat a close back below 1.0395 on the euro as the sign that the tariff pass-through has begun.

Macro Stance: China is stabilizing in the data but not yet recovering, and the tariff threat dominates. The Economist called it a moment of truth for Xi Jinping on deflation [28], and the early recovery signals come from factories rather than households. Trump has vowed an extra 10% on China alongside the Mexico and Canada duties [11], Beijing vowed all necessary measures against the new tariffs [29] and accused Washington of blackmail over fentanyl [30]. Consumers are cautious: sentiment lags even as blueberry sales boom [31].

PMIs & Activity: The official manufacturing gauge reached a three-month high in February [32], and the non-manufacturing PMI printed 50.4 for the month [33]. Reuters put the factory picture as activity picking up while trade uncertainties weigh [34]. The base is low: January’s official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.1 from 50.1 in December [35], and the Caixin reading showed growth slowing that month [36]. Activity is improving from a weak start, which is not the same as a recovery. A reading just above the 50 line is the one that matters for the credit cycle, since January’s print shows how quickly the index can slip back under it.

Credit Impulse: Policy is leaning on the banks rather than on large fiscal numbers. Reuters relayed a Bloomberg report of a $55 billion bank recapitalization [37], and it also reported that Chinese banks heeded a PBOC call to cut dollar deposit rates [38]. The yuan is the pressure valve: USD/CNY rose 1.45% over 20 sessions to 7.2853 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and regulators stepped up scrutiny of capital flows as the currency weakened [39]. A weaker yuan gives exporters room, and it gives the PBOC a reason to keep the banks cutting. The test is whether the recapitalization reaches the loan book, which is the next thing to watch.

Property: Property is still a drag, and the bottom is being argued over. Reuters said the decline in second-hand home prices narrowed for a seventh straight month [40]: a narrowing, not a turn. Hedge funds are positioning for a turnaround in the unloved sector [41], while the sale of Evergrande’s remains is being fought over in pieces [42]. Hong Kong’s bourse logged a 10% profit jump as trading turnover and IPOs surged [43], which is the offshore channel doing the work.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The trade lever is larger than the fiscal one. AP reported that Trump plans tariffs on Mexico and Canada while doubling the existing 10% tariffs on China [44], and Treasury’s Bessent urged Canada and Mexico to match US tariffs on China [45]. Mexico has proposed matching them [46]. Beijing is answering with trade and regulatory moves, targeting US agriculture [47] and requiring approvals for autonomous-driving software upgrades [48]. It also opened its telecoms sector to 13 foreign companies [49]: a reform signal aimed at the tech trade, not at the consumer.

Markets & Flows: The onshore and offshore markets disagree. On February 28 the Hang Seng closed at 22,941.32, up 13.4% over 20 sessions but down 3.3% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The Shanghai Composite at 3,320.90 gained only 2.8% over 20 sessions, and the CSI 300 ETF (ASHR) 0.8%. KWEB, the China internet ETF, is down 7.4% over five sessions at 33.93. Alibaba’s US shares rose 29.0% over 20 sessions to 132.51 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Retail money is there for the new listings: Mixue’s IPO drew a record retail subscription book of nearly US$206 billion [50].

New / Most Important: The most important signal is the AI capex, which is not waiting for stimulus. Chinese buyers are ordering Nvidia’s newest AI chips in defiance of US curbs [51], and Alibaba has set a US$52 billion capex plan that it sees as a catalyst for China’s big tech in the AI race [52]. Alibaba made its AI video model free to use globally [53], and Jack Ma is back in public view [54]. The pricing signal is in Hong Kong, where the AI trade sits and the listing pipeline is busy: Chinese tech firms are eyeing Hong Kong IPOs amid the DeepSeek-triggered AI boom [55].

Playbook ✓: Own the AI capex names through the offshore listings and keep China-domestic cyclicals underweight until the credit impulse turns. Alibaba’s 29.0% gain over 20 sessions shows the market is paying for the AI spend, and the Hang Seng’s 13.4% lift is the same trade in an index. Fade rallies in the onshore Shanghai index while the banks are being recapitalized rather than rewarded. ⚠ Divergence: the Hang Seng is up 13.4% over 20 sessions while the onshore Shanghai Composite is up only 2.8%, so the market is paying for AI and not for a broad recovery.

Macro Stance: The Bank of Japan has the inflation it wanted and a stronger yen working against it. The inflation rate climbed to a two-year high of 4% in January, which CNBC said supported rate-hike calls from BOJ members [56], and the Japan Times said inflation keeps the BOJ on its rate-hike path [57]. The BOJ chief warned of strong global uncertainty from US tariffs [58], which gives the bank a reason to move carefully. Growth is steady without being strong: fourth-quarter GDP beat forecasts on consumption and business spending [59], but CNBC said domestic consumption remains a worry [60].

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,155.50, down 5.7% over 20 sessions and 2.9% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The yen is the swing factor. USD/JPY closed at 150.0120 and is down 2.65% over 20 sessions, so the dollar has lost ground to the yen even as speculators pile in. Nikkei Asia reports the yen rally sputters despite unprecedented speculative interest [61], and Macquarie is bullish on the yen this year, though the rally may take a few more months [62]. The export-heavy and funding-sensitive names carry the cost. SoftBank closed at 8,273 yen, down 12.0% over 20 sessions and 6.1% in the prior session, while it was in talks to borrow $16 billion to fund AI [63] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Advantest is down 15.3% over five sessions at 8,116 yen (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).

Playbook ✓: Stay underweight the export-heavy Nikkei while the yen keeps its grip. The 5.7% slide over 20 sessions and the 2.65% fall in USD/JPY point the same way, and a close above 39,414.78, the index’s reference from January 29, would be the first sign it has found its footing (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Keep the chip-equipment and funding-heavy names out of the book, because SoftBank’s 12.0% fall over 20 sessions shows how the yen and the AI-funding trade interact.

Macro Stance: The Reserve Bank cut rates on February 18 and sounded cautious about more [64], and its governor said the bank did not want to start cutting too late [65]. The RBA itself warned of weak incomes and high inflation if productivity lags [66], which is the constraint on the next move. Treasurer Chalmers played down an uptick in underlying inflation [67], while the AFR wrote that he has damaged the central bank’s independence [68].

Demand & Financing: Housing has turned. CoreLogic data showed the Australian housing market ended its downturn as the rate cut lifted sentiment [69]. Global private-credit funds are set to storm the country [70], which means financing growth outside the banks. The currency is the weak point: AUD/USD closed at 0.6232, down 1.25% in the prior session and 2.68% over five sessions after a tumble on escalating tariffs [71] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The ASX 200 at 8,172.40 is down 4.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Fortescue lost 13.7% over 20 sessions at AUD 16.51 after iron ore logged a monthly loss on China steel export concerns [72].

Playbook ✓: Prefer domestic housing and banks to the miners. Iron-ore weakness is the cost in Fortescue, and the producers with the most China exposure carry the risk. Keep the Australian dollar short only while it sits below its 20-session reference of 0.6215 from January 31, because at 0.6232 on the last close it is still above that level (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).

Macro Stance: Growth is accelerating and the central bank is not in a hurry to help. GDP grew 2.9% in 2024, beating forecasts [73], and the latest reading was described as acceleration with more expected than delivered [74]: ‘Gospodarka przyspiesza, ale liczono na więcej’. The finance minister called 2025 a breakthrough year [75]. Inflation is the constraint. Business Insider Polska said inflation would rise further and gave the MPC a strong argument on rates [76], ‘Inflacja w Polsce jeszcze wzrośnie’. Bloomberg put the zloty at a 10-year high on February 27, fanned by a hawkish central bank [77]. Wages rose clearly in 2024 [78], ‘wyraźny wzrost’, and the unemployment rate turned up [79], ‘Stopa bezrobocia w górę’.

Markets: The zloty is the trade. Rzeczpospolita headlined that the zloty hit a seven-year record on February 24 [80], and Gazeta asked whether the NBP would intervene as the zloty turned ‘extremely strong’ while the euro and the dollar lost ground [81]. Santander warned that a strong zloty could weigh on GDP [82]. EUR/PLN closed at 4.1614, down 0.86% over 20 sessions, while USD/PLN at 4.0035 rose 1.55% in the prior session as the dollar bounced (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Equities have taken the strength. The WIG20 total-return tracker at PLN 49.00 is up 5.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and StockWatch said the WIG20 was back above 2,600 points, with Orlen, KGHM and Ukrainian names in play [83]. Bankier is asking how far the index is from its 2007 record [84].

Fiscal & Politics: Fiscal policy is under attack, not yet in the market. Leszek Balcerowicz said the government keeps spending that makes no sense [85], ‘Wydatki, które nie mają żadnego sensu’, and Bankier carried the same critique [86]. Rzeczpospolita asked whether banks are ready for Donald Tusk’s breakthrough [87], and a columnist wrote that the taboo on the 800+ benefit has collapsed [88]. The government’s own framing is the ‘Year of Breakthrough’ economic plan [89]. The political calendar now matters for the zloty. The presidential race has become a three-horse contest [90], and POLITICO reports that Poland’s nationalists stick to Trump ‘like glue’ [91].

Corporate & Sectors: Orlen is the dividend story. It proposed a record PLN 7 billion dividend for 2024 and the shares rose [92], and Bankier called it the national champion’s record cash stream [93]. The stock is up 16.6% over 20 sessions at PLN 62.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Bank Pekao earned PLN 6.4 billion and wants half of it for dividends [94]; the shares are up 6.0% over 20 sessions at PLN 170.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Dino Polska posted results and an all-time high as it grows in a weak market [95], and the stock is up 10.1% over 20 sessions at PLN 495.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). KGHM is the risk name. Tremors hit its Polkowice-Sieroszowice mine and injured a miner [96], a Chilean blackout also hit its mine there [97], and KGH is down 6.0% over five sessions at PLN 129.45 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). PZU named Andrzej Klesyk its new chief executive [98].

Geopolitics & Security: Security spending is a structural bid. The president has vowed to spend 4.7% of GDP on defence this year [99], Poland leased eight Apache gunships as a warm-up for a larger delivery [100], and Poland and Slovakia are teaming up on ammunition and weapons purchases [101]. Russian missiles hitting western Ukraine prompted Polish fighters to scramble [102], and a report found Russia paid operatives to paint anti-government graffiti in Poland [103]. The defence budget is also a fiscal argument, which is why the Balcerowicz critique [85] matters: the spending is political as well as military.

New / Most Important: The one signal that matters is the zloty. A currency at a seven-year high tightens conditions for exporters and squeezes bank margins, and Santander’s warning that it could weigh on GDP [82] puts the question directly to the MPC: is the strong zloty doing the disinflation work for it? The equity market has already decided that growth wins, as the Pekao and Dino moves show. The pace of the currency move, not its level, is what would change the call.

Playbook ✓: Own the domestic growth names, with banks and Dino as the core, and hedge the currency only above its reference. A EUR/PLN close above 4.1976, the reference from January 31, would mean the zloty has given back its 20-session gain, and the bank trade would need to be re-examined. Pekao is up 6.0% over 20 sessions at PLN 170.00 and Dino up 10.1% at PLN 495.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). ⚠ Divergence: the zloty’s strength and the bank rally argue for growth, but KGH is down 6.0% over five sessions, which says the metals and export-earnings side is breaking the other way.

Narrative: The consensus says AI spending keeps chips and software rising, and the tape is split between them. XLK is down 2.9% over 20 sessions at 225.53 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), even as Nvidia sold $11 billion of Blackwell chips in what it called its fastest product ramp [104]. Hardware is carrying the sector. Application software is not.

Reported: Salesforce missed on revenue and guided below expectations [105], and its stock fell after a weak annual forecast put AI monetization in focus [106]. Synopsys beat on forecast as AI chip demand lifted it [107], and Dell beat on full-year EPS [108].

EPS Upside Watch: The set-up favors the infrastructure names where demand is still the story. Synopsys’s beat [107] says the design-tool cycle is intact, and Nvidia’s own guidance remains the sector’s upside lever. The software laggards need a guide raise, not just a beat.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A record quarter did not lift the group. Nvidia’s beat-and-raise was met with a fall, as the S&P 500 ended down when Nvidia tumbled after its report [109], and the company’s stock is up only 0.2% over 20 sessions at 124.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).

Narrative: Meta’s product push is set against Alphabet’s slump. Meta is set to debut a stand-alone AI app during Q2 [110], and its stock at 668.20 is down 2.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Alphabet is down 15.2% over 20 sessions at 170.28, even as a bullish piece asks whether it is enroute to $10 trillion [111].

Reported: Warner Bros. Discovery added 6.4 million Max subscribers and forecast 150 million by the end of 2026 [112]. Paramount reported record subscriber growth [113], and Google announced layoffs in its HR and cloud units as part of ongoing cost cuts [114].

EPS Upside Watch: Streaming is where upside is being set, because the company is guiding to subscriber numbers, not just reporting them [112]. Meta’s AI app is a revenue option rather than a number, so any surprise rests on ad pricing that nobody has yet modelled in public.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Meta is paying its executives more while cutting 5% of its workforce [115], which points to margin discipline rather than AI spending. The market is not rewarding that discipline, while Alphabet is down 15.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), the reverse of the consensus that scale wins.

Narrative: The consensus is that deregulation and fee income lift the banks. XLF is up 2.8% over five sessions at 52.18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Bank of America’s chief said the bank will likely launch its own stablecoin [116].

Reported: Berkshire Hathaway posted record profit and its shares set a new high [117], although operating earnings surged and questions linger about its cash [118]. Goldman’s president joined the board in a rare promotion [119].

EPS Upside Watch: Upside comes from fee income, where stablecoins and the State Street–Apollo private-credit ETF are the new lines [120]. Spread income is the risk if the curve keeps flattening, and the bull flattening in Treasuries does not help net interest margins.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Regulators are pushing back on the new product, with US regulators raising concerns about the private-credit ETF in an unusual move [121]. The sector’s rally is being sold as deregulation, and the regulator response runs the other way.

Narrative: Oil is the consensus, and it is falling. WTI closed at 69.76 and is down 4.1% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Saudi Arabia may lower its April prices for Asia [122]. US drillers added oil and gas rigs for a fifth week running [123], while the energy ETF rose 1.55% in the prior session to 91.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).

Reported: EOG fell on lower 2025 free cash flow despite a fourth-quarter profit beat [124]. BP cut its renewables investment and boosted oil and gas [125], and Petrobras will issue dividends despite a fourth-quarter net loss of $2.8 billion [126].

EPS Upside Watch: Gas is the upside. Natural gas is up 25.8% over 20 sessions at 3.83 USD per MMBtu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and data-centre demand is driving it [127]. Producers with gas exposure are set up for upward revisions if the weather and supply story holds [128].

⚡ Breaking Convention: Crude fell while the energy ETF rose. WTI was down 0.8% in the prior session and XLE up 1.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The sector is trading gas and cash returns, not crude.

Narrative: Aerospace and power equipment are the consensus winners, and the tape disagrees on the electrical names. Rolls-Royce hit an all-time high on an upbeat outlook [129], and its upgraded forecasts sent shares soaring over 18% [130]. Meanwhile GE Vernova is down 12.5% over 20 sessions and Eaton 10.3% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).
Reported: Aixtron warned on revenue and its shares were on course for their worst day in a year [131]. EMCOR headed for its best one-day gain in a year on an upbeat Q4 and strong outlook [132].

EPS Upside Watch: Order books are the upside. ANA will buy at least 77 jets from Boeing, Airbus and Embraer [133], and Turkish Air says its Boeing order could take six more months [134], so timing rather than demand is the risk. Rolls-Royce and EMCOR show that guidance is being raised, which is what the sector needs.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Power equipment is being sold while the data-centre pipeline grows. Quanta is down 16.1% and Eaton 10.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), even as FirstEnergy’s five-year data-centre pipeline doubled to 3 GW [135].

Narrative: The consumer is the weak spot in the cycle. XLY is down 7.4% over 20 sessions at 215.96 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and US consumer spending posted its first drop in almost two years [6]. Consumer confidence fell by the most since 2021 [5].

Reported: TJX forecast annual sales growth and profit below estimates on muted consumer spending [136]. Domino’s missed on sales as a value-meal war tempered US demand [137]. Home Depot beat and broke its losing streak in comparable sales [138].

EPS Upside Watch: The exception is value and traffic. Yum Brands is near all-time highs as Taco Bell outpaces its peers [139], and Home Depot’s comparable-sales break is the sector’s upside surprise [138]. Upside needs the tariff noise to fade, and that has not happened yet.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A consumer boycott is visible in the headlines. A 24-hour ‘economic blackout’ was under way [140] and talk of a ‘Feb 28 Economic Blackout’ was spreading on social media [141], yet the S&P 500 is down only 1.9% over 20 sessions while Tesla is down 26.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).

Narrative: The defensives are the rotation. XLP is up 4.2% over 20 sessions at 83.08 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Morningstar asks whether the stock-market rotation now underway will last [142]. Investors who want a defensive income play are being pointed to staples ETFs [143].
Reported: Monster Beverage missed Q4 estimates [144], and Dole beat on revenue but lagged on EPS [145]. Unilever’s CEO turnover has drawn scrutiny [146].

EPS Upside Watch: Costco is the name the rotation favors. It is up 7.1% over 20 sessions at 1,048.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and a Yahoo piece calls it a top staples dividend stock [147]. Upside surprises need volume, and the consumer data are not yet showing it.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Monster missed while the group rallied. The defensive bid is not a fundamental beat story, which cuts against the consensus that staples are safe because their earnings are.

Narrative: GLP-1 pricing is the story, and branded supply is winning the argument. XLV is up 1.1% over 20 sessions, and Eli Lilly is up 11.8% at 920.63 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Lilly will spend at least $27 billion on new US plants [148] and has launched an ad campaign against weight-loss drug copies [149].

Reported: Teladoc tumbled after a wider loss and disappointing revenue guidance [150]. Madrigal’s quarter was strong with an even stronger outlook [151], and BofA raised its price target to $239 from $154 [152].

EPS Upside Watch: Madrigal is the estimate-revision name, since the move from $154 to $239 at BofA [152] is the signal. Lilly’s molecular-glue deal, potentially worth $1.25 billion [153], adds an option on the pipeline without changing the core story.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Hims & Hers plunged 22% on concerns about its weight-loss margins [154]. The compounding channel is being squeezed while Lilly is pulling its own prices down to fight for patients [155]. The market is paying for the branded side, not the compounding side.

Narrative: Copper is treated as an asset for grid and data-centre capex, and the consensus is a long-dated shortage. The industry needs $2.1 trillion of investment over the next 25 years [156], and Trump has ordered a new tariff probe into US copper imports [157].

Reported: Lynas Rare Earths’ profit collapsed as China kept a lid on commodity prices [158]. BASF banked on cost discipline [159], and Clariant’s core profit missed forecasts and its shares slumped [160].

EPS Upside Watch: The upside is in the metal, not the miners. Copper futures are up 5.28% over 20 sessions at 4.51 USD per lb (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and a tariff decision could lift the US price further. Newmont beat on higher gold production and prices [161], which is the template for a miner that beats on the commodity rather than on costs.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The miners lag the metal. COPX is down 2.2% over 20 sessions while copper futures rose 5.3% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The equity is not pricing the metal’s move, and that gap is the convention-breaker.

Narrative: Lower mortgage rates are the bid. The sector is up 3.95% over 20 sessions and 2.2% over five at 43.15 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Mortgage rates dropped to their lowest since mid-December [162], and that is the reason the rate-sensitive names have turned up.
Reported: American Tower’s stock declined 20% in the fourth quarter [163], which shows the REIT pain has been concentrated in the tower names rather than across the sector.

EPS Upside Watch: Demand is not yet confirming the rate bid. Pending home sales fell to a record low on weather and rates [164]. A sales rebound would be the upside signal for brokers and builders before it helps the REIT complex.

Growth data softened into the report date while markets priced a slower path rather than a recession. The January PCE index rose 2.5%, in line with expectations [[n7868]], and the Fed’s preferred core gauge hit 2.6% [[n6515]], so inflation is not what is breaking the tape. Activity is. The Atlanta Fed indicator put first-quarter growth on track to be negative [[n7881]], and its nowcast saw the economy shrinking after Friday’s data [[n6467]]. Households are pulling back: consumer confidence fell by the most since 2021 [[n7736]], spending posted its first drop in almost two years [[n6685]], and weekly jobless claims jumped to 242,000 [[n7853]]. Fourth-quarter GDP was still 2.3% annualized [[n7812]], so the slowdown is a late-winter story, not a finished one.
Rates & Curve

The 10-year Treasury closed February at 4.24% and the 2-year at 3.99%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 25 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28). Over 20 observations the 2-year fell 19 bps and the 10-year 28 bps, which leaves the spread 9 bps narrower. The curve is positively sloped and the move is a bull flattening, with the long end rallying more than the front. The five-observation move (2Y −20 bps, 10Y −18 bps; US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28) says the bid is recent and still running, and Bloomberg reported a Treasury rally that sent yields back below 4% as inflation cooled [[n8229]]. Equities did not follow the bonds. The S&P 500 closed at 5,954.50, down 1.9% over 20 sessions and 1.0% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The Nasdaq 100 is down 2.9% over 20 sessions, and the Russell 2000, at 2,163.07, is down 6.3%, the sharpest drawdown of the three. The VIX stands at 19.63, up 3.79 points over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and the dollar index at 107.61 is down 0.2% over 20 sessions but up 0.9% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).
New / Most Important

The tariff clock is the event to price. The administration has set March 4 for tariffs on Mexico and Canada, with the exact levels still to be set [[n3707]], and Trump has vowed an extra 10% on China over fentanyl in the same package [[n1135]]. Bessent says tariffs will not raise inflation [[n1289]], and that is the argument the bond market is buying: duties read as a growth tax rather than a price shock. Bessent has also promised an ‘affordability czar’ to deal with the cost effects [[n3724]]. For equities the threat already sits in the Russell 2000’s underperformance, which is where import-dependent and credit-sensitive companies trade.
Playbook ✓

Own duration into the jobs data and keep equity beta light. Activity is improving from a weak start, which is not the same as a recovery. A reading just above the 50 line is the one that matters for the credit cycle, since January’s print shows how quickly the index can slip back under it.
Credit Impulse

Policy is leaning on the banks rather than on large fiscal numbers. Reuters relayed a Bloomberg report of a $55 billion bank recapitalization [[n0987]], and it also reported that Chinese banks heeded a PBOC call to cut dollar deposit rates [[n1085]]. The yuan is the pressure valve: USD/CNY rose 1.45% over 20 sessions to 7.2853 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and regulators stepped up scrutiny of capital flows as the currency weakened [[n0985]]. A weaker yuan gives exporters room, and it gives the PBOC a reason to keep the banks cutting. The test is whether the recapitalization reaches the loan book, which is the next thing to watch.
Property

Property is still a drag, and the bottom is being argued over. Reuters said the decline in second-hand home prices narrowed for a seventh straight month [[n1273]]: a narrowing, not a turn. Hedge funds are positioning for a turnaround in the unloved sector [[n1090]], while the sale of Evergrande’s remains is being fought over in pieces [[n1121]]. AP reported that Trump plans tariffs on Mexico and Canada while doubling the existing 10% tariffs on China [[n1130]], and Treasury’s Bessent urged Canada and Mexico to match US tariffs on China [[n1216]]. Mexico has proposed matching them [[n1195]]. Beijing is answering with trade and regulatory moves, targeting US agriculture [[n1272]] and requiring approvals for autonomous-driving software upgrades [[n3074]]. The upside is volume in the cheaper EV leaders. Volkswagen’s ID.4 was the best-selling EV in Europe last month [[n6701]]. BMW (up 6.7% over 20 sessions) and the Volkswagen preference shares (up 5.5%) are the names where a volume beat would matter (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).
⚡ Breaking Convention

BYD is building a European footprint even as its German sales slump [[n6823]], and Tesla’s European sales almost halved last month [[n5712]]. European shares are rising over 20 sessions while the share of EVs is moving to Chinese brands, which is the opposite of the consensus that the incumbents are defending the market.
Narrative

The semis trade is AI demand against China share. SOXX is down 4.7% over 20 sessions at 208.52 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), with Chinese buyers ordering Nvidia’s newest chips despite curbs [[n1278]] while Nvidia warns of growing competition from Huawei [[n1104]].
Reported

Micron announced shipments of its 1-gamma DRAM [[n2124]], and Intel said new ASML machines are in production with positive results [[n5614]]. Intel also pushed its $28 billion Ohio chip factories into the next decade [[n6553]].
EPS Upside Watch

Korea’s memory names are the upside set-up. SK Hynix is down 4.5% over 20 sessions at KRW 190,200, while Samsung is up 4.0% at KRW 54,500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). DRAM shipments [[n2124]] and the Nvidia ramp are the demand catalysts that could reset the group’s estimates.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Nvidia’s record quarter did not lift the chip index. Nvidia tumbled after its report [[n0319]], and SOXX is down 6.9% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Shipments are running ahead of the stock price.

earnings_pattern.title: Earnings Pattern: What the Market Pays For
parts: Rewarded

Raised outlooks and cash returns get paid. Rolls-Royce hit a record after it raised its mid-term goals [[n2386]], and its shares rose over 18% on the upgrade [[n5035]]. EMCOR headed for its best one-day gain in a year on an upbeat outlook [[n4912]]. Snowflake’s big beat sent its stock higher [[n0314]], AB InBev’s shares jumped as higher prices lifted revenue and profit [[n2178]], and Berkshire’s record profit sent its shares to a new high [[n2001]].
Punished

Guidance that stops short gets sold. Salesforce fell after its weak annual forecast [[n2371]], and Nvidia’s optimistic forecast did not convince Wall Street [[n0317]]. Teladoc tumbled on a wider loss and disappointing guidance [[n2274]], and Sempra fell on a dour 2025 profit forecast [[n2141]]. Rocket Lab’s stock dropped despite a Q4 sales beat [[n5030]], Norwegian Cruise shares fell despite an earnings beat [[n2438]], and Keysight was the worst S&P 500 stock after its results [[n2289]].
Pattern

The pattern is guidance, not the quarter. Beats paired with raised outlooks were rewarded, as at Rolls-Royce and EMCOR. Beats paired with forecasts that failed to satisfy were sold, as at Nvidia, whose optimistic forecast did not convince Wall Street [[n0317]]. Revenue alone does not carry a share price. Nvidia’s sales grew 78% [[n0313]] and the stock still fell after the report [[n0319]].
Attention into EPS

The next test is margins and guidance again. Nvidia’s future margins were called a little concerning [[n2355]], and the sector debate has moved to AI monetization [[n2371]]. Dell’s EPS beat [[n0323]] and SoundHound’s revenue beat with an EPS lag [[n0324]] show how mixed the beats are. Super Micro’s surge after its delayed 10-K [[n4865]] was followed by a 26.1% slide over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), which is the same market reaction in a different name.
Playbook

Own the beat-and-raise and sell the beat-and-hold. Rolls-Royce’s record high on its raised outlook [[n2374]] shows what the reward looks like. Underweight or hedge the names whose guidance trailed the quarter, starting with Salesforce, and size into prints only where estimates are moving up. Nvidia is the test case for a beat that is not enough on its own: sales grew 78% [[n0313]] and the shares still fell on the report [[n0319]].

underowned.title: Rare earths beyond the Ukraine headline
parts: Attention Gap

Attention sits on Ukraine minerals and China’s curbs, not on the producers. Trump is demanding half of Ukraine’s rare earths [[n0864]], and the open question is whether a US–Ukraine deal would be a workaround to China’s curbs [[n1150]]. The minerals deal is still a proposal [[n7931]], so the equities are being valued on policy hopes rather than cash flow.
Exposure & Risk

MP Materials is up 10.44% over 20 sessions at 24.01 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Lynas (LYC.AX) is up 7.27% at AUD 6.79, after its profit collapsed as China kept a lid on prices [[n1008]]. The risk is a Chinese price response that compresses margins for the non-Chinese producers.
Trigger to Watch

A dated policy step is the trigger: a Chinese export-control move or the signing of the Ukraine minerals arrangement. Reuters has mapped the proposed deal’s mineral set [[n1011]], and the first concrete step on it would re-rate the group.

underowned.title: Copper miners lag the metal
parts: Attention Gap

Copper is discussed as an asset for grid and data-centre capex, while the miners are ignored. The industry needs $2.1 trillion of investment over 25 years [[n6495]], and Trump’s probe into copper imports [[n0940]] is a tariff story the producers have not been paid for.
Exposure & Risk

COPX, the copper-miners ETF, is at 38.22 and down 2.23% over 20 sessions, while Freeport-McMoRan at 36.91 is up 0.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The risk is that a tariff raises the US price while the miners’ cost base rises with the same investment cycle.
Trigger to Watch

The trigger is a US tariff decision that comes out of the probe Trump ordered [[n0939]]. If the decision lands, the copper-price gain of 5.28% over 20 sessions has a direct channel to the producers, and the gap closes quickly.

underowned.title: Uranium fuel, not just reactors
parts: Attention Gap

Nuclear is the AI-power story, but the fuel chain is ignored. Italy adopted a plan for a return to nuclear power [[n5077]], and a Saskatchewan paper argues Canada has to develop uranium enrichment to succeed in the new nuclear era [[n6484]]. Attention sits on reactors, not on the fuel cycle that feeds them.
Exposure & Risk

The uranium ETF URA is down 14.25% over 20 sessions at 24.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Cameco is down 12.45% at 44.04. Centrus, the enrichment name, is up 6.27% at 90.73. The risk is that the sector is sold on a call such as Jim Cramer’s ‘Sell it down here’ for Uranium Energy [[n6576]], which the tape can easily follow.
Trigger to Watch

A dated decision is the trigger: EDF has delayed its final investment decision on six new reactors to the second half of 2026 [[n4771]]. That delay pushes the fuel demand out in time, and the decision date is the test for the group.

underowned.title: Long Treasuries after the aversion
parts: Attention Gap

Attention has moved to duration only recently, as Goldman’s strategist says the aversion to bonds is over [[n8154]]. The long bond rally is still under-appreciated: TLT is up 4.63% over 20 sessions at 92.43, and the 10-year yield fell 28 bps over the same span (Yahoo Finance and US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28).
Exposure & Risk

TLT, the 20-year-plus Treasury ETF, and IEF, the 7–10-year ETF at 95.32 and up 2.31% over 20 sessions, carry the rally. Investment-grade credit (LQD, up 1.67% at 109.61) is the second leg. The risk is a tariff-driven inflation print that reverses the rally, and the Atlanta Fed’s negative growth readings [[n8183]] argue against that risk being large.
Trigger to Watch

The next US jobs data are the trigger, since Reuters says investor angst about the economy will be tested by them [[n0325]]. A 10-year close back above 4.52%, its level on January 30, would be the observable sign that the rally has stalled (US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28).

crypto.title: Crypto & Digital Assets
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 94,248.35 on March 2, up 9.55% in the prior completed daily close and 6.21% over five sessions, but still 3.27% below its February 10 reference over 20 sessions at 97,437.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-02). Ether rose 13.67% to 2,519.69 and Solana 24.23% to 178.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-02). Equities did not share the bounce. Coinbase is down 28.44% over 20 sessions at 215.62, Strategy is down 24.89%, and the bitcoin ETF IBIT is down 19.79% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Bitcoin fell 17.5% in February, its biggest monthly loss since 2022 [[n1596]].
New / Most Important

The new event is political, not technical. Trump named XRP, SOL, ADA, BTC and ETH as part of a US crypto reserve [[n1602]], and Bloomberg reported the rally that followed the naming [[n1612]]. Axios wrote that the naming sparked a $300 billion global crypto rally on Truth Social posts [[n1615]]. What the market has priced is the naming itself. The size and funding of any purchases are still open, which is why the named coins moved most.
Playbook

Hold bitcoin and ether against their 20-session references, 97,437.55 and 2,661.17, and treat the reserve bid as a test. A close above the bitcoin reference confirms the bid, and a close back below the March 2 print of 94,248 invalidates the bounce. Do not chase the 34% XRP session in the lead trade below. Use IBIT and Coinbase only once ETF flows turn positive, since both are still down about 20–28% over 20 sessions. Strong inflows into the ARK and Fidelity bitcoin ETFs ended an eight-day outflow streak [[n1584]], which is the first observable test.

flows.title: Capital Flows & Liquidity Framework
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is being set by central banks that are cutting slowly or not at all. The ECB may have to cut to a level that stimulates [[n2636]], while the BOJ chief is worried about tariff uncertainty [[n4052]] and the Bank of England’s Dhingra said gradual cuts would drag on the economy [[n2627]]. The Fed’s preferred gauge came in at 2.6% for January [[n6515]], which keeps policy patient. The PBOC pushed Chinese banks to cut dollar deposit rates [[n1085]]. Global debt reached a record high, raising the risk of bond vigilantes [[n7978]]. The policy bias matters more than the balance-sheet headlines. The ECB’s payment-system outage, which the bank has since fixed, was a reminder that plumbing matters too [[n2731]].
Rates & Dollar

The 10-year closed at 4.24% and the 10Y−2Y spread stood at 25 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28). Over 20 sessions the 10-year fell 28 bps and the 2-year fell 19 bps. The dollar index is at 107.61, flat over 20 sessions but up 0.94% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Long duration is the bid: TLT is up 4.63% over 20 sessions. The 2-year’s five-observation fall of 20 bps is the cleanest read that the front end is repricing for weaker data rather than for policy (US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28). Credit is calm in price: HYG is up 0.31% over 20 sessions at 80.13, and LQD is up 1.67% at 109.61. Gold is the dollar’s casualty, down 3.55% over five sessions at 2,848.50, as Reuters put it: gold set to record its worst week in three months on a robust dollar [[n8197]].
Credit Check

Private credit is the new leverage. Global debt reached a record high [[n7978]], and Bloomberg reported that bosses talk distress at the lowest level since before Lehman [[n2662]]. A State Street–Apollo private-credit ETF is launching, and US regulators raised concerns about it in an unusual move [[n6687]], which makes the product the first public check on the sector. Banks may be the unlikely beneficiary of the private-credit boom [[n5721]]. Japan is also cracking down on the booming market for JGB-backed loans [[n4088]], another credit channel regulators are now trying to close. High-yield (HYG, up 0.31% over 20 sessions at 80.13) and investment-grade (LQD, up 1.67% at 109.61) both finished higher over the period, which says credit has not yet been repriced for the growth scare (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).
Equity & Fund Flows

Positioning is short-term and defensive. Hedge funds ramped up bets on falling stocks [[n3086]], Berkshire liquidated its holdings in S&P 500 ETFs [[n8017]], and Steve Cohen turned negative because of DOGE and tariffs [[n2889]]. In crypto, spot bitcoin ETFs saw a record outflow of more than $1 billion in one day [[n1495]], and the first inflows in an eight-day streak followed [[n1584]]. In Hong Kong the retail appetite is visible in Mixue’s IPO book of nearly US$206 billion [[n4934]]. Morgan Stanley published its list of the most crowded hedge-fund trades [[n2920]], and crowded lists are where unwinds start.
Portfolio Implication

Keep duration and cut equity beta into the tariff date. The events are the March 4 tariffs [[n3707]] and the next jobs data [[n0325]], and the flows say the bond bid has more room than the equities. Hedge the Russell 2000, down 6.26% over 20 sessions, rather than the S&P 500, down 1.92%, because small caps carry the tariff and credit risk (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Bitcoin ETF flows are the first read on whether the reserve bid turns into a flow or stays a headline [[n1584]].

anticipatory.title: March 4 tariffs on Mexico and Canada
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing a threat with the levels still open. Trump vowed March 4 tariffs for Mexico and Canada, plus an extra 10% on China over fentanyl [[n1135]], and the commerce head said the exact levels are still his to set [[n3707]]. The dollar index at 107.61 is up 0.94% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), so part of the tariff is already in the currency. Mexico has proposed matching US tariffs on China [[n1195]], which pulls the trade chain into the deal.
Conditional Expression

If the levels arrive at the threatened size, the dollar extends and cyclicals lag, with the Russell 2000’s 6.26% fall over 20 sessions the first casualty. If Washington sets lower levels, the dollar gives back the five-session gain and the duration rally has room to continue. In either case the position sizing should follow the level, not the headline.
Risk

The risk is a retaliation chain. Beijing is targeting US agriculture [[n1272]], and Beijing has pledged all necessary measures [[n1073]], so a tariff step on March 4 [[n1135]] would not stay inside North America.

anticipatory.title: The next US jobs report
parts: What Is Priced

The jobs report is pending, and investors are anxious about it. Reuters said rising angst about the economy will be tested by the US jobs data [[n0325]]. The 10-year at 4.24%, down 28 bps over 20 sessions, shows the market already leans toward a softer labour market (US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28).
Conditional Expression

A soft print extends the bull flattening, with the 10-year leading (down 28 bps over 20 sessions against 19 bps for the 2-year), and the S&P 500, down 1.92% over 20 sessions, struggling to hold 5,954.50. A hot print reverses the bid, and the 10-year would need to clear 4.52%, its level on January 30, to say the rally has ended.
Risk

The consumer data are already soft. Spending posted its first drop in almost two years [[n6685]], and jobless claims rose to 242,000 [[n7853]]. A jobs print that looks strong only because of a claims spike would be a misreading of growth, not growth itself.

anticipatory.title: A 25% tariff on the EU
parts: What Is Priced

A threat with a timeline set by the president’s own words. Trump said 25% tariffs on the EU would be announced soon [[n8162]], and the Guardian quoted him calling the bloc formed to screw the US [[n8064]]. The Euro Stoxx 50 is up 3.34% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), so the market is not pricing the full threat.
Conditional Expression

If the duty is announced at the threatened size, EU cyclicals lead the fall and the euro weakens. If it is deferred, the DAX’s 3.77% gain over 20 sessions extends into a deal narrative. The defence names are the hedge in both cases, with Rheinmetall already up 33.24% over 20 sessions.
Risk

The risk is retaliation and domestic politics. A divided German electorate complicates the Merz plan for defence [[n2759]], and S&P’s outlook cut on France [[n2770]] adds a second front to any trade fight.

anticipatory.title: A Ukraine plan that needs Washington
parts: What Is Priced

The defence trade is pricing a peace plan that still needs the US. Europe agreed steps toward peace in Ukraine but needs US backing [[n3668]], and UK and European leaders are drafting a plan to take to Washington [[n3729]]. Rheinmetall closed at EUR 1,006.50, up 33.24% over 20 sessions and 12.56% over five, while the US aerospace and defence ETF ITA is down 1.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).
Conditional Expression

A US-backed plan moves the defence trade from the Rheinmetall bid to the rest of the sector, and the 20-session gain could partly unwind. A collapse in talks keeps the premium and lifts the European defence ETFs. Lockheed Martin, down 2.02% over 20 sessions at 450.37, is the US read-across to watch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28).
Risk

The defence trade has already run hard, with Rheinmetall up 12.56% over five sessions. The risk is a headline peace deal that removes the premium at speed, leaving the position with the cost of the move and none of its upside.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — Blackwell ramp outruns the stock
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia sold $11 billion of next-generation Blackwell chips in what it called its fastest product ramp [[n2238]], and Chinese buyers are ordering its newest chips despite US curbs [[n1278]]. BofA says the stock could jump more than 50% as the chipmaker remains in a dominant position [[n6773]]. The thesis is that the demand is real and the stock has not yet paid for it.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The close is 124.92, up 0.22% over 20 sessions and down 7.07% over five after the report (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The hurdle is the 20-session reference of 124.65. The risk is the margin debate: Nvidia’s future margins were called a little concerning [[n2355]].
Trade Expression
Buy shares on a close above the 20-session reference, or a call spread over the coming months. Invalidation is a daily close below 124.65.

catalysts.title: $BABA — capex and free models
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Alibaba’s US$52 billion capex plan [[n0976]] and its free global AI video model [[n0970]] put the group at the centre of China’s AI race. Jack Ma’s return to public view [[n1237]] adds a sentiment tailwind. The thesis is that the spend is the moat.
Price Hurdle & Risk

BABA closed at 132.51, up 28.98% over 20 sessions but down 7.82% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), with the 20-session reference at 102.74. The risk is policy, since Washington is also pressing tariffs on China [[n1130]].
Trade Expression
Buy shares on a pullback that holds above the 20-session reference. Invalidation is a daily close below 102.74.

catalysts.title: $LLY — branded GLP-1 wins the price war
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Lilly is spending at least $27 billion on US plants [[n3366]] and running an ad campaign against weight-loss drug copies [[n6510]]. Hims & Hers warned it may stop selling compounded weight-loss drugs [[n4779]], and its shares plunged on looming compounding curbs [[n4841]]. The thesis is that compounding curbs push patients toward the branded product.
Price Hurdle & Risk

LLY closed at 920.63, up 11.83% over 20 sessions and 5.37% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Lilly is also cutting Zepbound vial prices for self-pay patients [[n2099]], which is the risk to margins.
Trade Expression
Shares, with adds on a hold above the 20-session reference of 823.23. Invalidation is a close below 823.23.

catalysts.title: $META — an AI app and fewer people
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Meta is set to debut a stand-alone AI app during Q2 [[n2444]], and it is cutting 5% of its workforce while lifting executive bonuses to 200% [[n2223]]. The thesis is that cost discipline pays for the AI spend, but the revenue case for the app is unproven.
Price Hurdle & Risk

META closed at 668.20, down 2.74% over 20 sessions and 2.25% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), with the 20-session reference at 687.00. The risk is that the app takes longer to monetize than the stock needs.
Trade Expression
Neutral on shares, with a collar around 668.20: long the stock, short a call above 687.00. Invalidation is a daily close above 687.00, which would turn the collar into a bullish position.

catalysts.title: $TSLA — Europe and the Musk drag
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Tesla’s sales almost halved in Europe last month and it was surpassed by a Chinese rival [[n5712]]. Protesters gathered at showrooms against Musk’s role with DOGE [[n6805]], and Tesla owners vented their anger [[n6085]]. The pending step is the California ride-hail bid against Waymo and Uber [[n2379]]. The thesis is that brand damage is compounding faster than the product cycle can answer.
Price Hurdle & Risk

TSLA closed at 292.98, down 26.81% over 20 sessions and 13.27% over five, after a 3.91% bounce in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). The 20-session reference is 400.28. The risk is a sharp squeeze on any political reset.
Trade Expression
A put spread below 292.98, sized small. Invalidation is a daily close above 400.28, the 20-session reference.

catalysts.title: $RKLB — the short report and the Neutron date
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Bleecker Street Research shorted Rocket Lab and said it had materially misled investors [[n4903]], and the stock sank on the short report and doubts about its Neutron rocket [[n4862]]. Rocket Lab reaffirmed a 2025 first launch of Neutron [[n5091]], and the shares still tumbled 13% [[n5090]]. The thesis is that the launch date is the test, and the short case now has a date attached.
Price Hurdle & Risk

RKLB closed at 20.49, down 28.18% over 20 sessions and 12.99% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), with the 20-session reference at 28.53. The risk is a launch on schedule, which would squeeze the shorts.
Trade Expression
A put spread or a short position, sized small. Invalidation is a daily close above 28.53, the 20-session reference.

spec.retail_intro: The dominant popular-narrative trade is the crypto-reserve rally, in which Washington’s naming of XRP and Solana sent both coins surging, the same reflexive mechanics that drive any speculative run in which a rising price becomes its own argument.

retail.title: XRP / XRP-USD — the reserve coin Trump just named
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story retail tells itself is short. The government has named a crypto reserve, XRP is on the list, and a coin whose issuer was among the cases the SEC has dropped is now named as part of the reserve. Decrypt’s roundup of the biggest crypto cases dumped by the SEC runs from Coinbase to Ripple [[n1605]], and XRP holders are likely to read that as vindication. The emotional hook is the flip: TheStreet reported that XRP had become the third-largest crypto, passing Tether [[n1620]]. Round numbers such as $3 tend to be the levels traders anchor on, and the 2.94 close sits just below it (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-02), with the 20-session reference at 2.42.
What Is Driving It

XRP rose 34.07% in the prior completed daily close to 2.94, up 26.55% over five sessions and 21.23% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-02). The move was the reserve list: CoinDesk reported that Trump named XRP, SOL, ADA, BTC and ETH as part of the US crypto reserve [[n1602]], and CNBC’s headline listed bitcoin, Solana, XRP and more [[n1614]]. Solana rose 24.23% in the same session to 178.50, Dogecoin 15.85% and Ether 13.67%, while bitcoin rose 9.55% to 94,248.35 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-02). The backdrop is the wrong one for a rally. Over 20 sessions the S&P 500 fell 1.92% and the VIX rose 23.93% to 19.63, while the 10-year yield sat at 4.24% after falling 28 bps (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28; US Treasury, prior close 2025-02-28). A crypto-only bid when equities are weak is a flight to a story, not to safety.
The Social Signal

Stocktwits flagged that Solana had hit a year low in retail sentiment on February 25, as bitcoin’s crash rippled through the market [[n4891]], less than a week before the reserve surge. Axios wrote that Truth Social posts sparked the rally [[n1615]], and the Economic Times put the meme-coin mood plainly: the hype fizzles as Trump cashes in, and fans are left wondering whether the pump was just another [[n5125]]. Retail appetite has not gone. Fortune India said Pi Coin had skyrocketed 242% since debut [[n1428]], and Business Insider called meme coins hot right now [[n1480]]. A Business Insider writer who went to a major bitcoin conference as a skeptic concluded that buying the dip was worth the risk [[n1580]].
Historical Analog

The closest analog is a mechanism rather than a single episode: a rising price becomes the argument. Each leg is taken as proof the thesis was right, and buyers who arrive after a visible endorsement need the next leg to keep working. The first wave is the informed or institutional buyer and the second is the crowd chasing a named asset. The danger is the one that comes after: once the endorsement stops being news, the second wave is what is left holding the coin.
Smart Money View

Institutions are split on pace and on which coins deserve a place. For the trade, BlackRock added its bitcoin ETF to a model portfolio for the first time [[n1530]], and Standard Chartered still sees bitcoin hitting $500,000 despite the selloff [[n1496]]. Against it, spot bitcoin ETFs saw a record outflow of more than $1 billion in one day [[n1495]], the Swiss National Bank’s president said bitcoin is not a worthy reserve asset [[n1570]], and Coinbase’s Brian Armstrong favors bitcoin alone as the best option for a reserve [[n1600]]. Flows then turned: TradingView reported that ARK 21Shares and Fidelity’s bitcoin ETFs ended an eight-day outflow streak with strong inflows [[n1584]]. The disagreement is about which tokens belong in a reserve and how fast the money follows, not about whether the reserve is positive for crypto. Desks are likely to sell strength in the names outside bitcoin.
When the Narrative Breaks

Use the levels. The reserve trade holds while XRP stays above its 20-session reference of 2.42, because a fall through that level would erase the whole 21.23% gain. The round $3 is the next test, and a close back under 2.94 would lose the momentum. Solana must reclaim its 20-session reference of 200.36 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-02), and bitcoin’s 97,437.55 is the test for the whole complex. The instrument risk is that XRP moved 34% in one session, so liquidity can vanish on a retracement. The dollar index at 107.61 is up 0.94% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), and Mexico and Canada tariffs are due March 4 [[n3707]], which tightens the bid for risk assets. The mechanism that ends the trade is simple: when the naming stops being news, the crowd is the last buyer.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — is $700 still on the table?
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Tesla is the stock holders tend not to abandon. Owners are angry: protesters gathered at showrooms against Musk’s DOGE role [[n6805]], and Tesla owners vented their anger [[n6085]]. The bull case is still on the table, since Barron’s asked whether the stock could reach $700 a share on outstanding execution [[n2483]]. Holders who read the brand damage as political tend to expect it to pass. Bloomberg’s headline that investors are bracing for more losses [[n2457]] shows the institutional nerves, a warning that dip-buyers typically dismiss as noise.
Where It Breaks

The trigger is the 20-session reference of 400.28, and the stock is at 292.98, down 26.81% over 20 sessions and 13.27% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28). Europe is the observable. Business Insider reported in late February that Tesla’s sales almost halved there the month before [[n5712]]. The instrument risk is that a 26.81% fall over 20 sessions leaves retail buyers underwater, so a second leg below 292.98 would test the holders who bought the dip.

retail.title: IonQ / IONQ — a million bucks by 2030
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The pitch is blunt. 24/7 Wall St. asks whether IonQ can rocket you to a million bucks by 2030 [[n5065]], and the Motley Fool offers seven quantum stocks that could supercharge a portfolio [[n4825]]. Amazon’s Ocelot quantum chip gave the story a big-tech badge [[n4981]]. Quantum is easy to sell as the next AI, and IonQ is the simplest name to hold it through.
Where It Breaks

IonQ closed at 24.57, down 36.69% over 20 sessions and 22.59% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), with its 20-session reference at 38.81. The instrument risk is dilution. IonQ announced $500 million in at-the-market funding alongside its results [[n4924]], and it is in discussions to buy ID Quantique for about $250 million [[n4928]]. A close above 38.81 would be the first sign the reference is back in play, and a loss of the 24.57 close would invite further selling. Quantum names tend to be bought on the story before the revenue, so a sell-off in the story can run steeper than the fundamentals alone would suggest.

retail.title: Leveraged chip ETF / SOXL — big bets on market moves
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Leveraged ETFs are gaining in popularity as a way to make a big bet on a view. CNBC reports that investors are gravitating to funds that allow big bets on market moves [[n4772]], and its interview with Direxion’s chief describes a growing appetite for leveraged and inverse funds [[n4770]]. The hook is leverage on a single view: semis up or down, three times over.
Where It Breaks

SOXL closed at 22.73 after a 21.10% five-session fall and 16.28% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-28), with its 20-session reference at 27.15. Bloomberg reported that Koreans who plowed into leveraged ETFs were burned as Tesla’s shares fell [[n5043]]. The instrument risk is decay in a 3x product on a choppy tape, plus thin liquidity when the crowd exits together. Leveraged funds reset daily, so a 20-session decline is compounding rather than a single move, which is how a pullback traps late buyers. A close back above 27.15 is the signal that the leveraged crowd is winning again.
